runtime_inputs: Calibrated RGB-D, public goal, robot proprioception and robot-only IK; no object truth

cube_worksite_height.interpretation: The observed cube center lies half a learned cube height above its support; its applied nominal tool offset is 0.6 of that measured height. Thus the nominal target is cumulative support height plus 1.1 cube heights, rather than 1.4. If visual finger geometry chooses a higher pickup offset, preview that measured planned offset explicitly.

findings: Lowering thin-prism grasps alone did not reliably improve complete success and regressed previously successful cases.
Seed906 was falsely rejected by an overstated cube worksite tool height; the corrected preview passed physical seed906.
Baseline903-905 had real 6-10mm bottom gaps and no robot/support contacts at the final attempted release; tool height settled roughly4-6mm below commanded pose.
The source-height recovery waypoint could descend at a tall destination before moving sideways; the parent integrated a separate safe-clearance correction.
A one-seed successful worksite check is not a broad success-rate claim.

portable_provenance.verification: Every copied trial goal, candidate hash, outcome, metrics, error, sensor and order was checked against its recorded result.

comparison_limits: Adaptive development groups differ and reuse seeds/baselines, including records present in other reports. No combined success rate or independent generalization claim is supported.
offline_diagnostic_boundary: The original offline truth diagnostics are preserved as diagnostic evidence only. Simulator object poses, contacts and dimensions were never runtime policy inputs.
